properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-25, ruling on twelve of the thirty-three leaf parts `unallocated_component` reported as holding no function.

═══ WHAT THEY ARE ═══

`sub:tool-surface` holds twelve slices — ask, assure, built, capture, claims, coherence, exchange, ingest, operate, query, skills, temporal. Each is one file under `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/`, and each EXPOSES over MCP a family of functions that core modules implement. `tools/temporal_tools.rs` realizes four capabilities and all four are allocated to `cmp:temporal`; `tools/skills_tools.rs` realizes two and both are allocated to `cmp:skills`.

═══ THE RULING ═══

**A slice's function is the capability it exposes, and that capability belongs to the module that implements it.** These twelve are therefore correctly empty: the design says what they are for by saying what they carry, not by giving each one a function of its own.

Two alternatives were put and declined:

① **Give each slice its own capability** — twelve nodes of the form "expose the temporal tool family over MCP". Declined as over-modelling: it describes plumbing rather than product behaviour, and inflates the capability count by 6% with nothing a reader would act on.

② **Allocate the exposed capability to the slice as well as the implementer** — closes the finding with no new nodes, and was declined for the reason that matters most here: it would deliberately fuse the surface with the subject. `dec:the-two-oversized-subsystems-are-split-functionally` separated Finding from Telling precisely so a part that finds a problem is not the part that decides how loudly to report it, and `dec:reflow2-is-built-for-observability` is why. Allocating an implementer's function to its own surface undoes that cut one edge at a time.

═══ THE COST, STATED ═══

⚠️ **This ruling did not, on its own, make the finding go quiet.** `detect_unallocated_components` did not consult a parking ruling when this was written, though `unsatisfied_requirement` and `unreviewed_ideas` both did — so twelve deliberately-empty parts kept reporting as defects. That inconsistency was fixed in the same session rather than worked around, per the standing rule that a mistake is corrected at its cause.
properties.name: DECIDED — the twelve tool-surface slices are surface, not implementer: they hold no function of their own
properties.rationale:
Recorded as one decision covering all twelve because they share their method and their justification exactly — one surface, cut once by lifecycle phase, every slice standing in the same relation to the modules behind it. Twelve nodes would duplicate the reasoning and let one drift.

The alternatives are written into the decision rather than discarded because a later reader running span-of-control or allocation checks over `sub:tool-surface` will find twelve empty boxes and needs to meet the reason rather than re-derive it — the same argument that kept the tool surface at twelve members instead of splitting it to reach seven.
